title: Deadlock on Parent-Child Thread Lifecycle Shutdown
pattern: A parent thread signals a cooperative producer-consumer child thread pair to shut down, then blocks waiting to join them. The producer thread exits quickly, leaving the consumer thread blocked forever waiting on a channel read from the dead producer.
why_bad: The consumer thread never reaches its shutdown check, causing the parent thread to hang indefinitely during join operations.
detection: Spawning interdependent threads where shutdown triggers are set, but parent thread joins are executed sequentially without join timeouts.
counterexample: Closing the communication channel explicitly before joining, which automatically unblocks the consumer thread with an `End-Of-Stream` error.
fix: Never block on joins without timeouts, or use non-blocking channel reads, or ensure the channel itself is closed to unblock the consumer thread.
